example: A definition named `glossary.first_parent_history` declares the phrase "first-parent history". A term reference to that name renders the phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to the declaration, without displaying the identifier or a badge. {cite}`requirements.definitions.references`
rationale: The example is a concrete case. Its input is a definition named `glossary.first_parent_history` with the phrase "first-parent history", plus a term reference to that name. It states three outcomes: the phrase is rendered, as an ordinary hyperlink to the declaration, with no identifier or badge shown. `tests/definitions.rs#fn[a_term_reference_renders_only_its_phrase_as_a_plain_link]` builds exactly this scenario. The glossary chapter declares `first_parent_history` with `:phrase: first-parent history`. The guide chapter contains "Follow the {term}`glossary.first_parent_history`.". The test then makes these assertions: - **Rendering, plain link, no identifier or badge.** It uses `assert_eq!` on the whole trimmed guide content, expecting exactly `Follow the first-parent history.`. The phrase is the only link text. No class, badge image or other markup is allowed, and the identifier `glossary.first_parent_history` cannot appear as visible text. A shields.io badge or a displayed identifier would make the equality fail. - **Link to the anchored declaration.** The href points at `glossary.html#habeas-definition-glossary.first_parent_history`. The test also asserts that the glossary chapter contains `id="habeas-definition-glossary.first_parent_history"`, so the link target exists. `tests/definitions.rs#fn[phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved]` adds coverage from the referenced `requirements.definitions.references`: - The phrase is escaped: `*alpha* & ` renders as `*alpha* & <beta>`. - There is no badge: the test asserts the content has no `shields.io`. - The link has the right relative href from a nested chapter, and there is exactly one such link. - Inline-code references, fenced-code references and escaped references stay literal. Together the two tests check each outcome in the example and the cited requirement's rendering obligations. I found no gap.

text: A definition named `glossary.first_parent_history` declares the phrase "first-parent history". A term reference to that name renders the phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to the declaration, without displaying the identifier or a badge. {cite}`requirements.definitions.references`

The `{term}` role followed by a backtick-delimited full definition name MUST reference a named definition. In rendered Markdown, the reference MUST display the definition's phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to its anchored declaration, without a badge. The phrase MUST be escaped appropriately for rendering.

Missing targets and targets of another kind MUST be reported. Escaped references and references in Markdown code examples MUST remain literal. A term reference MUST NOT satisfy a requirement citation or a Rust function's requirement-coverage obligation.
